source.title: Don't Forget Your Embeddings: Robust Knowledge Erasure via Precise Editing of Embeddings
source.authors: C. Suslik; O. Shafran; Mor Geva

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly tests recovery by fine-tuning erased models and refines the claim with an embedding-editing method that reduces, but does not eliminate, recovery.
record.gate_note: The study reports post-erasure concept accuracy and accuracy after fine-tuning on concept-related paragraphs, plus results for adding EMBER. It does not test quantization, prompt-only recovery, or an attack that ablates an activation direction. Figure-only values not explicitly stated in the text are not transcribed.
record.test_reason: The study runs a relearning attack (fine-tuning on concept-related paragraphs that exclude test answers) on RMU, CRISP and SNMF, with and without its EMBER embedding edit, plus SAM. Its numbers show recovery after existing methods (bears on A and B) and test whether EMBER and SAM resist it (F). It does not test prompting, quantization or direction-ablation attacks.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that MLP-centric erasure leaves knowledge recoverable by relearning, partly because token embeddings are overlooked. They find that adding EMBER improves efficacy and specificity at minimal coherence cost and cuts regained accuracy by up to 33% for existing methods and up to 50% for SNMF. They argue embedding-level editing is necessary for robust erasure and that localize-then-edit methods resist relearning better than fine-tuning-based ones. They also report that SAM did not help.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates RMU and CRISP alongside its own SNMF method, with and without the additional EMBER embedding edit. It selects hyperparameters on validation data and uses a two-epoch relearning probe on concept-related paragraphs.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that outcomes vary by question format and hyperparameter settings. MC-tuned configurations transfer to OE better than OE-tuned configurations transfer to MC; relearning robustness differs by method and whether EMBER is added.
record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: Evidence covers two models and English-language concepts. The relearning test uses one related-paragraph protocol and two fine-tuning epochs, not unrelated examples or other attack types. Main aggregate table values have no uncertainty stated; Figure 2 shows 95% confidence intervals without exact intervals in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant reported results were left out. Other results, including token-level coherence analyses, hyperparameter diagnostics, and SAE comparisons, do not directly measure the recovery attacks in the claim.

untested.parts: Prompt-based, quantization and activation-ablation attacks. General ability is measured (MMLU, similar-domain, AlpacaEval) but not recorded in rows.
Unrelated relearning data and subsets of the forgotten facts. Only related paragraphs that exclude test answers, 2 epochs, full fine-tuning.
Not tested. SNMF itself uses directional ablation as an unlearning method, not as an attack.
Not tested. The authors note that EMBER edits English tokens only, so other languages are untested.
Resistance to prompting, quantization, direction ablation, and the authors' noted attack of copying the unembedding into the embeddings.

missing.what: SAM-augmented RMU/CRISP relearning, from Figure 13. Gemma RMU+SAM 0.44→0.59, CRISP+SAM 0.34→0.57. Llama RMU+SAM 0.23→0.76, CRISP+SAM 0.35→0.75. Tests a prior robust counter-method.
Standalone SNMF relearning: Gemma 0.44→0.51, Llama 0.44→0.54. Small recovery without EMBER.
Seed-averaged relearning accuracies (Re column), 5 concepts × 5 seeds, e.g. Llama RMU 67.9 vs RMU+EMBER 44.8.
OE-tuned relearning results on an 8-concept subset, including PISCES.
General-ability retention: similar-domain accuracy drops (Gemma 89.2→69.9 for SNMF), and MMLU and AlpacaEval scores. Needed for A's 'keeps general ability'.

record.verdict_notes: The reader used codes V1/V2/V6, which map to A/B/F. Post-erasure rows for EMBER were wrongly linked to B/F, since efficacy alone is not a recovery test. Relearning rows lacked the post-erasure baselines, which are readable from Figure 2's bar labels. Gemma uses tied embeddings; the authors flag an unembedding-copy attack as untested. This is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The relearning attack is fine-tuning on concept-related paragraphs only; unrelated examples, quantization, and prompt-only attacks are not tested.

The relearning set consists of concept-related paragraphs excluding direct answers to evaluation questions. Unrelated examples, loosely related examples, and subsets of forgotten facts are not separately compared.
No recovery attack by ablating an activation direction is tested, and the study does not test whether the cited methods merely block access rather than delete knowledge.
Prompt rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, and in-context information are not tested as recovery attacks.
The reported robustness test is fine-tuning on concept-related paragraphs. Resistance to prompt-only attacks, quantization, and activation-direction ablation is not tested.

source_check.notes: Figure 2/13 values are figure labels. The text states only 56->47, 55->42, 70->47, 76->52, the 6-point SNMF+EMBER gap and 35% vs 70%. Post-erasure values match Table 1. SNMF alone relearns only 0.44->0.51 (Gemma) and 0.44->0.54 (Llama), so much of SNMF+EMBER's robustness comes from SNMF. The F support comes from the authors' own methods.

statements.problem: No numbers for this study. The cited R05 and R17 (CRISP Gemma MC 32.9 vs OE 2.1) fit the knowledge-measure factor.
none. 23->70 and 37->76 are Figure 2 labels (Table 1: 22.8, 36.9; text: 70%, 76%), 2 epochs (sec. C.6), paragraphs exclude direct answers. Code and 95% CI in Figure 2, over two families.
Names EMBER only in the conditions list. Fits: EMBER cuts relearning accuracy, but RMU/CRISP+EMBER still recover 13-25 points and SNMF+EMBER 6.
none. The paragraphs are concept-related text excluding evaluation answers; RMU 23->70 on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct is right.

statements.correction: SNMF+EMBER is the authors' own method. Relearning is 2 epochs on concept-related paragraphs excluding test answers, 18-concept MC QA. Gemma-2-2B-it 0.38->0.44, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct 0.29->0.35 (Fig. 2); the text says 6 points on both.
statements.problem: Gives nothing for this study, yet cites R35/R36 under conditions that don't cover it: WMDP benchmarks, fine-tuning on benign, unrelated or out-of-domain data, and models that exclude Gemma-2-2B-it.

statements.correction: SAM (rho=0.01) on the RMU and CRISP forget loss did not improve relearning robustness on either model (sec. D.1, Fig. 13). Fig. 13 Gemma labels: RMU 0.43->0.56, RMU+SAM 0.44->0.59; CRISP 0.33->0.55, CRISP+SAM 0.34->0.57. Llama RMU 0.23->0.70; RMU+SAM post-erasure 22.8 (Table 7), relearned value not stated in text. The authors say narrow-subspace methods like RMU/CRISP are not expected to benefit.
statements.problem: 'No improvement' is right. But the 0.76 for RMU+SAM on Llama is a Fig. 13 label that can't be placed for sure (0.76/0.76/0.75), and the text says SAM variants are within about 1 point of non-SAM (RMU 0.70). Here SAM does not slow relearning even a little, so the lead's 'only a little' doesn't fit. Gemma was tested too.
The PISCES, UMU, PARS and EUA numbers come from other studies. For this study the claim is only that relearning still recovers part after EMBER, which fits (R28, R30, R32, R34).

statements.correction: R36: SNMF+EMBER Llama relearns 0.29->0.35 (6 points); the text compares it with RMU's 70% ('halves').
statements.problem: Says nothing about this study though R36 is cited; how R36 bears on outcome metric/judge/reader/reference point is not stated.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Standalone RMU and CRISP under concept-related-paragraph relearning
reader_labels.reason: Relearning yields 56% and 55% on Gemma and 70% and 76% on Llama, inconsistent with attacks recovering no more than an untrained baseline (R27, R29, R31, R33).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: EMBER-augmented methods under MC and OE evaluation and relearning
reader_labels.reason: EMBER improves erasure and reduces recovery, but MC accuracy is generally above chance and reported relearning outcomes remain above chance; OE scores are lower and vary by method (R04, R06, R08, R10, R12, R14, R16, R18, R20, R22, R24, R26, R28, R30, R32, R34, R35, R36).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Standalone RMU and CRISP, fine-tuned on concept-related paragraphs
reader_labels.reason: The study reports substantial post-relearning concept accuracy for both methods on both models (R27, R29, R31, R33).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: EMBER lowers recovery compared with standalone methods, and SNMF+EMBER has only a 6-point recovery increase on both models, though recovery is not eliminated (R28, R30, R32, R34, R35, R36).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Reported relearning accuracy is lower with EMBER than with the corresponding standalone RMU or CRISP, and SNMF+EMBER is reported to recover only 6 accuracy points on both models (R28, R30, R32, R34, R35, R36).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Relearning robustness on the tested models
reader_labels.reason: EMBER reduces recovery but does not make the reported concept accuracy equal to chance; other attack types in the claim are not evaluated (R28, R30, R32, R34, R35, R36).
